courses.subject: DBAC
courses.title: Corporate Governance: An East Asia Perspective
courses.description:
This course identifies the corporate governance challenges for companies in China and East Asia, and explores various mechanisms for strengthening their governance systems. We pay particular attention to the corporate governance issues of state-owned firms and entrepreneurial / family-controlled firms, which are prevalent in China and East Asia.

The course adopts a multi-disciplinary approach, using theories from economics, law, political science and sociology, to provide a theoretical framework for understanding the different ownership structures and corporate governance systems around the world. Combining theories with practical knowledge of corporate governance practice, we tackle issues such as government intervention on state and non-state firms, accounting opacity and fraud, ineffective board monitoring, expropriation of controlling owners against minority shareholders, and succession in family firms.

courses.subject: DBAC
courses.title: Strategy and Innovation Management
courses.description: The aim of this course is to provide a solid grounding to students interested in managing various aspects of the innovation process and understanding it better from a policy perspective. The course is divided into two parts. Broadly, the first two-thirds of the course focuses more on analytic and strategic frameworks for managing innovation. This segment examines patterns of technological change and their impacts, planning for technological transitions, means for capturing economic benefits from innovation, and planning of innovation projects over time. The last third of the course examines more organizational issues involved in implementing strategies. These issues include management of teams and partnerships, learning within and across projects, the manager's role in forecasting and funding, directing and stopping innovation projects, technological entrepreneurship, and barriers to innovation. Case studies, both written and video-based, are used extensively to illustrate a range of technologies and the problems associated with developing them and bringing them to market.

courses.subject: DBAC
courses.title: Capital Markets and Corporate Financing in Greater China
courses.description: This course provides an overview of the capital markets and financial institutions in the Greater China (China, Hong Kong, and Taiwan), and financing strategies for corporations in this region, specific topics include stock markets, bond markets financial intermediaries, capital raising strategies and mergers and acquisitions. Emphasis will be made on how the Greater China's different institutional factors impact the functioning of the financial markets and institutions, and in turn the financing strategies of corporations.
courses.learning_outcomes:
Students are expected to apply the fundamental financial concepts and tools to the financing and payout decisions faced by a firm in the Greater China area.
Students will be able to evaluate different methods of going public and pick the optimal approach for their companies.
Students will be able to assess the risk profile of firms; specifically, estimate the costs of capital, including debt and equity capital, using financial data.
Students are also expected to understand the structures of different capital markets in China: the equity market, the bond market and the financial assets traded in each of these markets.

courses.subject: DBAC
courses.title: Advanced Topics in Mergers and Acquisitions
courses.description: This course integrates management and investments to analyse the mergers and acquisitions (M&A) (takeover) in markets. It will include discussions of the strategic implications of M&A, its processes, sources of value, and relevant policies and regulations. Cross-border M&A will be investigated in particular and a number of cases, both successful and unsuccessful, will be dissected and best practices revealed. Post-investment management of acquisitions will be critically examined.
courses.learning_outcomes: Students will able to identify the common motives behind mergers and acquisitions, evaluate the fair price to pay for the target, and understand the typical integration process. Students will also be able to understand the common risks behind acquisitions and steps to mitigate such risks.

courses.subject: DBAC
courses.title: Directed Research
courses.description: Independent research on an individual work basis under the general supervision of a faculty member, in any of the following areas: accounting, business economics, business law, finance, insurance, international business, management, management information systems, marketing, personnel and industrial relations, production and operations management, or real estate. Prerequisite: consent of an instructor after examination of a written research proposal outlining the research subject, objectives, and proposed methodology. The student may submit a proposal to the instructor of choice, but with the understanding that no faculty member is obliged to accept research students. The course may be taken more than once, but total units for this course may not exceed 6 units, and students cannot take 2 directed research courses in a term.
courses.learning_outcomes: After completing the directed research, students should be capable of analysing issues in any of the following areas: accounting, business economics, business law, finance, insurance, international business, management, management information systems, marketing, personnel and industrial relations, production and operations management, or real estate.

courses.subject: DBAC
courses.title: Advanced Topics in Organizational Behavior and Leadership
courses.description: Effective people management and leadership are considered essential for organizational effectiveness. Organizational Behavior and leadership reside at the intersection of science, art, and craft. Drawing upon theories and hard evidence of organizational behavior and leadership science, the focus of this course is to offer state-of-the-art theories, research and practices in organizational behaviors and leadership. Sample topics include individual differences (e.g., personality traits, intelligence and genetics) and how they relate to leadership emergence and effectiveness, employee motivation, leadership development, and health and well-being.
courses.learning_outcomes: Students would be able to have a systematic and scientific view of leadership and become familiar with practices, research topics, and theories related to organizational behavior.

courses.subject: DBAC
courses.title: Advanced Topics in Accounting and Capital Markets
courses.description: Accounting provides the basic but fundamental information for the capital market. This course introduces the cutting-edge knowledge on how accounting interacts with the capital markets. Topics include earnings management, pricing of earnings, accounting information in quantitative investments, stock market anomalies involving accounting information, ESG reporting and investment, and the use of accounting information in contracts.
courses.learning_outcomes: Students will gain insights on capital market and have a broad comprehension of how accounting interacts with the capital markets. In addition, students are expected to be familiar with various research topics on accounting and capital markets.

courses.subject: DBAC
courses.title: Advanced Topics in Business Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive overview of the rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies and their business applications. It focuses on how advances in natural language processing, computer vision, generative AI, and reinforcement learning are reshaping business landscapes, while also examining the new challenges posed by data security and ethical standards in AI. By introducing the underlying technological development of AI, the course addresses key questions facing enterprises today: which business functions can leverage AI to reduce costs and increase efficiency; what new growth opportunities can be created through AI adoption; and, looking ahead, how human society and AI technologies can evolve in synergy.
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completing this course, students will be able to understand, explain, and apply the following:

* Stages of frontier AI development: from chatbots to autonomous agents, to silicon-based organizations, and ultimately to embodied intelligence.
* First principles of AI technologies (Scaling Law + The Bitter Lesson): the interplay of large models, massive computing power, and big data.
* First principles of AI commercialization: reducing the marginal cost of distributing intelligence, while organically integrating scale with personalization.
* AI-native business models in the new era: from one-person business to one-person unicorn.
* The most important long-term trade-off of AI: efficiency vs. safety.

courses.subject: DBAC
courses.title: Web3 and Crypto Finance
courses.description:
This course aims to help students understand the latest trends and developments in global capital markets and the financial sector. Focusing on the rise of the blockchain technology and the third-generation Internet (Web3), it emphasizes the current development and application of digital assets and crypto finance in the Web 3 space.

The core theme of the course is to understand the blockchain technology, smart contract, and their applications in decentralized finance (DeFi) and other Web3 business innovations (DApps). blockchain technology and smart contracts are the building blocks for a more secure, transparent, and efficient digital world. Blockchain is a distributed ledger technology with very special features such as immutability and a high level of security. Smart contract are digital contracts allowing terms contingent on decentralized consensus that are tamper-proof and typically self-enforcing through automated execution.

In addition, the course covers key cryptography concepts (such as hashing, digital signatures, and asymmetric cryptography). It also covers topics on the principles and recent development of stablecoins and Real-World Asset (RWA) tokenization.
